children: President Donald Trump's announcement of a security deal with Greenland lifted Critical Metals shares and other stocks linked to the Danish territory Monday.

Shares of Critical Metals rose 35% to $9.10; shares have risen 30% this year. Greenland Energy stock surged 126% and Greenland Mines stock skyrocketed 136%. The broader Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.2%.
Critical Metals has a market capitalization of $1.3 billion, well above that of Greenland Energy at $120 million, and Greenland Mines at $22 million.

Trump said Friday he reached an agreement with Denmark and Greenland that granted the U.S. "permanent control" over Greenland's security, ending his threats of annexing the territory. While details are limited, investors reacted positively to the prospects of the U.S. gaining access to Greenland's mineral reserves.
The Trump administration has invested in rare earths over the last year to cut reliance on China for materials required in key defense equipment.

Critical Metals announced in April the Greenland government approved the transfer of the remaining stake in the Tanbreez mining project to the firm. Critical Metals holds a 93% stake in the project, while European Lithium-whose Sydney-traded shares rose 14%-holds the remaining 7%.

Tanbreez is one of the world's largest rare earth hard rock deposits at 45 million tons, with more than one-fourth of that tonnage in heavy rare earth oxides, which are used in defense, clean energy and technology applications.

Greenland Mines is developing a mining project in southeast Greenland the firm said will tap one of the world's largest palladium, gold, and platinum deposits. Greenland Mines has 80% ownership of the project.
Greenland Energy, a Texas-based company, said last month it would postpone a planned oil drilling project in eastern Greenland until winter 2027, citing a delay in permit approval.
